free_tier.stated: "Trial access: Try the service, prototype and validate applications and services. The EGI grant includes up to 4 vCPU cores, 8GB of RAM and 100GB of block storage." The service runs on the federated infrastructure of the EGI Federation and is part of the EGI EOSC Node offering, with standard API access to virtual machines carrying guaranteed resources.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: A 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 100 GB VM is exactly the shape that fills the gaps other records leave: the HPC programmes here allocate wall-clock on a queue, and this gives an always-on address, so the pair composes into a control node that submits to a batch system and keeps state.

limits.value: The trial is capped at 4 vCPU, 8 GB of RAM and 100 GB of block storage, and it is requested through a contact form rather than self-service, so a human decides when the grant starts and what it renews into.

notes: The smallest allocation and the only one that is a real virtual machine rather than a queue slot or a web tool, which is why it is recorded despite being small. The identity is a contact form and an email, with no institutional sentence on the page read, so the practical gate is a human reply rather than a policy. Duration and renewal terms for the trial are not published on the page read, so no expiry is recorded rather than guessed. What would settle the verdict is submitting the form; the page names no eligibility criteria to test against.
